identity.name: Vegetable carbon
identity.chemical_class: Carbonaceous food colour additive (insoluble particulate carbon)

function.mechanism: Black particulate carbon provides colour through broad light absorption/scattering as a pigment.

adi.basis: EFSA ANS re-evaluation reported insufficient data to assess safety; no numerical ADI identified from accessible EFSA material in this session.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA ANS Panel reported available data were insufficient to assess safety of vegetable carbon (E153), citing lack of reliable exposure data and oral toxicology data.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database record for VEGETABLE CARBON lists 'NO ADI ALLOCATED'.

notable_bans: United States: provisional listing of carbon black (impingement/channel process) for use in food, drugs, and cosmetics terminated in 21 CFR 81.10(g).

concerns.summary: Rat studies reported altered vasomotor/endothelial responses after repeated intragastric/oral exposure to food-grade vegetable carbon or carbon black particles.

Review literature reports oxidative DNA damage signals after gastrointestinal exposure to insoluble particles including carbon black, though causality and relevance at food exposures remain uncertain.
IARC classifies carbon black as Group 2B (possible carcinogenic hazard), and an older rat model reported co-carcinogenic signal under high-fat + chemical-carcinogen conditions.

no_concern_confirmed: A 2022 radiolabelled toxicokinetic rat study found near-complete fecal recovery after oral gavage and no quantifiable systemic translocation beyond GI/lung compartments under study conditions (PMID: 36242080).

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical EFSA or JECFA ADI available in the accessed records; exceedance cannot be quantitatively assessed.

risk_assessment.rationale: Evidence is mixed: EFSA reported insufficient data to confirm safety, U.S. CFR history is non-supportive for food-use carbon black, and animal oral studies show vascular/oxidative signals; however, recent oral toxicokinetic work suggests minimal systemic uptake under test conditions.
key_factors: EFSA 2012 re-evaluation concluded available data were insufficient to assess safety
WHO JECFA record: NO ADI ALLOCATED (evaluation year listed as 1987)
U.S. CFR 81.10(g) termination language for food-use provisional carbon black listing
Animal oral studies indicate vascular and oxidative-stress-related effects
Recent rat toxicokinetic study shows minimal oral systemic translocation
